pr_title: Prevent ipv6 discovery messages for Sonos
pr_body:
## Proposed change
Sonos Integration does not support ipv6.  Ipv6 discovery messages were causing error and stack dump.

- reject autodiscovery messages with ipv6 addresses
- log warnings if ipv6 addresses are received (for example from the Sonos network topology messages)

issue_context.title: Sonos IPv6 discovery exception
issue_context.body:
### The problem

I am receiving an error during startup of an unhandled exception.

```
2025-03-01 22:42:14.859 ERROR (Recorder) [homeassistant] Error doing job: Task exception was never retrieved (None)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/Users/paulus/dev/hass/core/venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/soco/core.py", line 332, in __init__
    socket.inet_aton(ip_address)
    ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^
OSError: illegal IP address string passed to inet_aton

The above exception was the direct cause of the following exception:

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/Users/paulus/dev/hass/core/homeassistant/components/sonos/__init__.py", line 498, in _async_handle_discovery_message
    await self.async_subscribe_to_zone_updates(discovered_ip)
  File "/Users/paulus/dev/hass/core/homeassistant/components/sonos/__init__.py", line 211, in async_subscribe_to_zone_updates
    soco = SoCo(ip_address)
  File "/Users/paulus/dev/hass/core/venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/soco/core.py", line 120, in __call__
    cls._instances[key][args] = super().__call__(*args, **kwargs)
                                ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/Users/paulus/dev/hass/core/venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/soco/core.py", line 334, in __init__
    raise ValueError("Not a valid IP address string") from error
ValueError: Not a valid IP address string
```

When I print the IPs that are being passed in, I receive an IPv6 address for one of my Sonos Symfonisk Lamp Gen 1. Soco lib doesn't like this.

AFAIK, ipv6 is not supported.  That said it should handle the error better 

Does the lamp also have an ipv4 address on the network?

You state this happens during the auto discovery?

Please turn on debug logging for the integration and attach.

Context would be helpful also, what changed that caused this to occur.

a) just plugged this device in
b) just switched over to an ipv6 network
c) just upgraded HA
....

Has the speaker been working in HA already? Do you have other Sonos device that are available?

If the integration is setup the diagnostic file will be helpful as this will have the Sonos network topology in it.

zeroconf needs a filter here https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/d006d33dc0b940aecbf3bdf4526b1e1d62aaf9b7/homeassistant/components/sonos/config_flow.py#L27

I suggest borrowing this one https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/d006d33dc0b940aecbf3bdf4526b1e1d62aaf9b7/homeassistant/components/doorbird/config_flow.py#L170

@bdraco - yes, that's probably simplest for the short term.

@balloob if your sonos device is actually speaking IPv6 and you feel adventurous; would you mind reviewing https://github.com/SoCo/SoCo/pull/976 / seeing what else breaks?

review_comments: There are multiple ways to get into this entry point besides auto-discovering. Including sonos topology messages and direct entries in the configuration.yaml. So we'll shut those down here; rather than call SoCo and get the stack dump.
I think we shouldn't log this. Especially in discovery, we can just ignore it.
Further analysis indicates we can get to this function via SSDP discovery. Changing the messages to debug.
